title: Hosted API quick-slate: interactive code + model preview tiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a compact set of getting-started screenshot assets that demonstrate model selection, the inline request builder, and language-specific code snippets (JS/Python/cURL). This ticket covers final art export, alt text, copy proofreading, and a small set of annotated overlays for docs and the console help panels.
goals: Provide a 3-card quick-slate visual kit: Model preview, Request composer, Code playground
Ensure assets work as single-frame screenshots and as 16:9 hero images for docs
Include accessible alt text and annotations for developer docs and onboarding flows
acceptance_criteria: Three exported PNGs in both light and dark themes, optimized for web and docs
Copy matches the latest API names and param examples in docs (confirmed with PM)
All images include alt text and a short caption for docs use
Design reviewed and approved by PM and an engineering reviewer (performance/accuracy of displayed payloads)
Filenames follow naming convention and live in Drive under the onboarding-redwood-hostedapi folder
design_notes: Model preview card should surface model name, latency estimate, and a small example prompt + sample output (truncated). Keep output under 3 lines to avoid overflow.
Request composer shows: prompt field, system message toggle, temperature slider at 0.2, tokens estimate badge. Use compact token counter style used across console.

Code snippet tile includes 3 tabs stacked visually: JavaScript (fetch + streaming comment), Python (requests or httpx), cURL example. Use short, copyable snippets with placeholders for API_KEY and MODEL.
Provide small annotation arrows for 3 callouts: model pin, streaming toggle, and quota meter. Callouts should be subtle and disabled for docs hero images but present in the detailed export.
Dark theme exports must maintain contrast ratios (WCAG AA) for overlay text and badges. Use token badge accent from design tokens (neutral-700 on light / neutral-100 on dark).
Avoid marketing copy; use literal product copy for accuracy (e.g., 'Models: redwood-alpha-1 / gpt-compatible-3b').
